title: To The Editors Of The Editorial Page Of The Wall Street Journal Regarding “Potheads Head For The Emergency Room”. Dehumanizing Others Dehumanizes Yourself
description: As I previously confessed, I have been reading the Journal and its editorial pages for over sixty years (even longer than I have smoked marijuana),...
content_html_sanitized:
As I previously confessed, I have been reading the Journal and its editorial pages for over sixty years (even longer than I have smoked marijuana), because I believe that it plays an important part in the capitalist system that upholds individual freedom.

 

Mea culpa. It was with great sadness and frustration that I eventually discovered that the Journal had rejected libertarianism in favor of a “reefer madness” level of Prohibitionism regarding cannabis.

 

The December 9th Opinion headline, Potheads Head for the Emergency Room “Two new studies show that the ill effects of THC are increasing.”

 

That was simply a slur too far.

 

Oddly, it wasn’t until the last two paragraphs that you referenced the subject of the headline, cannabis hyperemesis syndrome, a very strange phenomenon in which an anti-emetic suddenly became a powerful hyperemetic, hitting heavy cannabis users without any warning or explanation. A classic example of a paradoxical effect, which in any other context you would not mock but rather you would insist on the necessity of medical research.

 

Or would you go to a cancer ward and mock cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy and vomiting violently until they smoked very illegal marijuana? Would you mock  AIDS patients who were anorexic and starving to death until very illegal marijuana gave them the “munchies”?

 

Would you mock disabled veterans, who still cannot get legal access to treat their chronic pain from their wounds they got defending your right to mock their use of cannabis?

 

Actually, do the Editorial Page Editors read the Wall Street Journal? You really should. It’s a great paper, despite its editorial pages’ occasional hyperreefermadness emesis.

 

For example, on July 31st the Journal published some truly great journalism, ‘Combat Cocktail’: How America Overmedicates Veterans.

 

It begins, “To treat PTSD, the Department of Veterans Affairs put hundreds of thousands of patients on multiple streams of powerful medications despite suicide risk.”

See

The Wall Street Journal Carries Excellent Story About The Outrageous Medical Abuse of Veterans: But No Mention of Medical Cannabis

 

But why was there no mention of medical cannabis?

As I said, “I have to wonder if the Journal editors would allow such heresy.” It is certainly newsworthy.

See

Veterans for Medical Cannabis Access

“Veterans For Medical Cannabis Access or VMCA, advocates for veterans' rights to access medical cannabis for therapeutic purposes.”

And from the DAV : Disabled American Veterans Medical Marijuana's Uses and Benefits for Veterans

 

Would you mock children? Just last month the Journal printed a truly horrifying article about the effects of over medication of children by the medical profession.

See

Millions of Kids Are on ADHD Pills. For Many, It’s the Start of a Drug Cascade

 

Let me emphasize that I have never advocated that anyone, adult or child, use marijuana, medically or recreationally, but neither have I advocated that anyone, adult or child, be arrested for doing so.

 

After 30 million arrests, can the Journal’s editors say the same?

See

How Many Americans Will Be Arrested While You Are Reading This Article?

And

The Many Risks of Politicized Psychiatry From Woodstock to Artificial Ignorance

And

Questions About Addictions and Mental Illness. Confusing Cause and Effect.

And

History of Cannabis Use and Cognitive Function In Older Adults Lifetime cannabis users performed better across all cognitive domains.

And from 1999

New York Times Runs Pro-Medical Marijuana Op-ed By National Review Senior Editor Richard Brookhiser
